methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective multicenter study (5 centers) with landmark analysis at 6 months. Clear inclusion/exclusion criteria and Cox proportional hazards model with assumption validity checking documented. Limitations acknowledged: retrospective design with inherent selection bias; 6-month landmark analysis excludes rapidly progressive patients (<6 months), artificially inflating observed OS (35 months vs historical 11-22 months for chemo-ICI). Imaging heterogeneity: 37% of patients evaluated with different modality at baseline vs 6 months; RECIST 1.1 feasibility with PET-CT quality-dependent and not fully characterized.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual cohort study (2b per Oxford CEBM). Clinically relevant to mNSCLC management: DpR at 6 months inversely correlates with mortality (HR 0.31 for >60% shrinkage, group 1 did not reach median OS; HR 2.14 for progression/minimal response). Findings support existing clinical practice of pursuing maximal tumor response. However, conclusions largely confirmatory: association between radiological response and survival well-established in oncology; study applies known principle to specific population without introducing new therapeutics or strategies.

reporting_quality.justification: Adequate STROBE adherence with comprehensive demographic tables (Table 1) and response-stratified patient characteristics (Table 2). Multivariate Cox model with clear adjustment variables (histology, PD-L1, brain metastasis, number of metastases). Limitations: supplementary figures/tables referenced but links redacted; IRB approval noted (IRB 2024-02) but institutional review board specifics not verified; primary protocol/data sharing statement absent; imaging modality switching (37% different type) noted in text but not systematically reported in supplementary table; median follow-up 27.7 months clearly stated.

novelty_literature.justification: Incremental confirmation of well-established principle. Association between tumor response (ORR, DpR) and survival outcomes extensively documented in prior literature (cited studies include KEYNOTE-189, IMpower150, CheckMate series). Study applies existing concept to specific subpopulation (mNSCLC on first-line chemo-ICI). Claims regarding 6-month DpR as 'predictor' lack mechanistic novelty; finding aligns with prior work on radiological response prognostication. No new biomarkers, mechanisms, or therapeutic approaches introduced.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-structured manuscript with clear sections. Demographic and baseline characteristic tables (Table 1-2) comprehensively presented with appropriate statistical tests. Survival curves (Figure 1) effectively communicate OS differences across response groups. Multivariate results (Table 3) clearly displayed with hazard ratios and 95% CIs. Discussion appropriately contextualizes against landmark trials (KEYNOTE, IMpower150, CheckMate-017/057). Minor issues: some citation density in introduction; redundant emphasis on prognostic value across sections. Overall publication-ready quality.

key_strengths: Multivariate Cox model with clear adjustment for confounders (histology, PD-L1, brain metastasis, number of metastases) and documented proportional hazards assumption verification
Comprehensive patient stratification and demographic reporting across four response groups with appropriate statistical testing (ANOVA, Fisher's exact, chi-square)
Clear quantification of survival differences: group 1 (deep response) median OS not reached vs group 4 (progression) 16.6 months (HR 0.28-0.32)
Large multicenter cohort (175 patients from 5 institutions) improving generalizability compared to single-center studies
key_concerns: Retrospective design with acknowledged selection bias; landmark analysis at 6 months excludes early progressors, artificially inflating OS estimates to 35 months (far superior to historical 11-22 month outcomes from KEYNOTE/IMpower trials), limiting real-world applicability

Imaging heterogeneity: 37% of patients evaluated with different modality at baseline vs 6 months; RECIST 1.1 reliability with PET-CT quality-dependent but not systematically characterized or reported in supplementary table

Limited novelty: findings confirm well-established association between tumor response and survival; no new biomarkers, mechanisms, or therapeutic strategies introduced. Study applies known principle to specific subpopulation without advancing field understanding

Data transparency gaps: supplementary figures/tables references redacted; no explicit data sharing statement or protocol availability; clinical trial registration not mentioned despite retrospective design
Predominantly adenocarcinoma cohort (82.3%) limits extrapolation to squamous NSCLC; authors acknowledge this limitation but analysis does not formally stratify squamous subset outcomes
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 3 paper: competent retrospective analysis with appropriate statistical methods confirming prognostic value of early DpR in mNSCLC, but limited novelty and selection bias from landmark analysis inflating OS estimates. Recommend minor revisions addressing imaging heterogeneity documentation and data sharing transparency before acceptance at Tier 3.
